summary: Targeted 8 load-bearing claims from brief.md: job-board segment match (thin, brief's own Risks flag a size mismatch with FellowScript's small-church audience), faith.tools as the top reach channel (single source, zero traffic/usage data), SmartGroups' free tier as a proven objection-handling structure (competitor's own pricing page only, no conversion evidence), the EdTech teacher-champion analogy applied to volunteer leaders (cross-domain inference bridging paid professionals and unpaid volunteers), the Subsplash 'another app' fatigue claim (sole source is a commercially interested vendor), the screen-free-church objection (single advocacy article, prevalence unknown), the Sept/Jan pitch-timing claim (11-15 year old sources describing congregant recruitment, not tool pitching), and vendor-reported ecosystem scale numbers (self-reported, unaudited). These were chosen for being load-bearing to the identify/reach/pitch success criteria, resting on corroboration_count 1 or single commercially-interested sources, or stated more confidently in the brief's prose than their sourcing supports.
